original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: On the PR #7041 length-42 block word, mask (4) has no realizing pair. The same holds after every adjacent transposition, including the exchange of string indices 17 and 18 named by open question 1 of PR #7226. The unrestricted six-source depth-two question at c=7 stays open.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers one released edit inside the c=7 depth-two handoff: the index-17 boundary swap of the block word, which PR #7226 states and does not evaluate. A new operation is not the missing step.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. Mask (4) is one of the four weight-1 masks the block word misses; showing that the named boundary edit still misses it removes that one-letter repair.
stop_rule: Stop once every adjacent transposition, including index 17, is shown to miss mask (4), or stop if any incident pair reads as that mask.
evidence: Written one-prefix argument plus an exhaustive standard-library census: 903 pairs of the unswapped word, 9 unequal adjacent boundaries, and 32 equal-letter identities. For index 17 the only moved prefix is q'_18 = (2,1,7,1,6,1), and the only two count vectors that would read as mask (4) against it are absent. Exactly two readings change, both to non-readings.

open_questions.question: Which of the 17 weight-3 masks missed by the unswapped word appear after exchanging indices 10 and 11?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is open question 2 of PR #7226. This census only tracks mask (4), so it does not say whether the 2/4 boundary creates a missed weight-3 mask.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate those 17 masks on the single word obtained by swapping indices 10 and 11.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing algebraic. The weight-3 predicate is not implemented in this package.

open_questions.question: Does a non-adjacent transposition of this block word realize mask (4)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Adjacency is what keeps the edit to one prefix. Two moved prefixes can cooperate, so the adjacent miss does not bound a general transposition.
open_questions.first_step: Swap one pair of indices at distance 2 whose letters are 4 and 0, and rerun the 903-pair predicate.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The full domain is the 861 transpositions, which this census does not enter.
